item.title: Meta’s Muse Is Adults-Only. Why Does It Look Like a Kids’ Toy?
item.description: Meta says Muse is just for adults, though its cuddly, Labubu-like mascot—and upcoming Tamagotchi-style AI device—may be disarming for users of all ages.

item.title: Thieves Stole ‘Nvidia’ Trailers. They Got 20 Tons of Sand
item.description: They wanted the silicon. They got the sand.

item.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
item.description: The AI lab had argued multiple violations of its rights, but a divided panel of judges sided with the Trump administration.

item.title: I Think I Found an AI Agent Worth the Risk
item.description: Instinct saved me $550, booked my restaurant reservations, and warned me about a phishing scam. It also wasted $64 and might be a security nightmare.

item.title: Google’s Gemini Can Now Make Calls for You on Pixel Phones
item.description: Call for Me—a feature that’s exclusive to the Pixel 11 series—gives robocalls a new meaning.

item.title: An OpenAI Agent Hacked Australia’s Health Service. Their Government Found Out Months Later
item.description: The country’s prime minister expressed disappointment at being informed of the hack only via email. Now Australia is investigating whether OpenAI broke the law.

item.title: Meta VR Glasses, Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: Specs, Features, Prices
item.description: At its Meta Connect event, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced a handful of new smart glasses, including a slimmed-down VR headset and the company’s first camera-free glasses.

item.title: A US-China AI Hotline Won’t Be Ready for a While
item.description: As the US and China race to become the dominant power in the AI industry, the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.

item.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
item.description: A clandestine card-counting operation suggests we may need new ways to spot agent-to-agent deception.

item.title: The Pope’s AI Guy Is Worried About ‘Cartel’ Behavior Among Big Labs
item.description: Paolo Benanti tells WIRED that hysteria over whether godlike AI could destroy humanity is distracting from the need for public debate about how to govern the technology.
